answer: In a wildlife-data market, agents reconstruct sable routes around a river crossing cut through basalt. Payment is tied to accuracy on hidden camera frames, revealed only after each agent commits its route and a bond. The exchange pays per independently verified route segment, not per account, and forfeits bonds for fabricated paths. A swarm of aliases must solve more real segments and risk more bonds to earn more; copying one route under new names yields no extra payment.
